questions.question: A family has an annual income of Rs. 8,00,000, out of which they save some money. They spend 15% of the total income on health. The expenditure done on education is half of the expenditure incurred on rent. The expenditure on food was Rs. 40,000, which is 10% of the expenditure on rent. How much money (in Rs.) is saved?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A family has an annual income of Rs. 8,00,000

They spend 15% of the total income on health

The expenditure done on education is half of the expenditure incurred on rent

The expenditure on food was Rs. 40,000, which is 10% of the expenditure on rent

**Concept Used:**

A percentage is a number or ratio that can be expressed as a fraction of 100

**Calculations:**

According to the question,

⇒ 10% of rent = 40000

⇒ 100%= Rs. 400000

Expenditure on rent = Rs. 40,000

⇒ Expenditure on education = (Expenditure on rent)/(2)=(400000)/(2) =Rs. 200000

⇒ Expenditure on health = 15% of total income = 800000times(15)/(100)=Rs. 120000

⇒ Total expenditure= 400000 + 200000 + 120000 + 40000 = Rs. 760000

⇒ Savings = Total income - Expenditure = 800000 - 760000 = Rs. 40000

**Hence, The money he saved after all the expenditures is Rs. 40000**

questions.question: X, Y and Z enter into a partnership. X invests some money at the beginning. Y Invests thrice the amount of X after 4 months and Z invest double the amount of Y after 9 months from the beginning. If the annual gain be Rs. 450000, then what is the share of Y?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Profit ratio = (Capital × Time)

X : Y : Z = (1 × 12) : (3 × 8) : (6 × 3) = 12 : 24 : 18 = 2 : 4 : 3

Total profit ratio = 2 + 4 + 3 = 9 parts

9 parts = Rs. 450000 ⇒ 1 part = Rs. 50000

Share of Y = 4 parts = 4 × 50000 = Rs. 200000

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 200000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total annual gain = Rs. 450000

Y joins after 4 months and Z joins after 9 months from the beginning.

**Formula Used:**

Profit Ratio = Investment × Time

 
 Partner X
 Capital = P | Time = 12m
 Profit = 12P

 
 Partner Y
 Capital = 3P | Time = 8m
 Profit = 24P

 
 Partner Z
 Capital = 6P | Time = 3m
 Profit = 18P

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the initial investment of X = P

⇒ Investment of Y = 3P

⇒ Investment of Z = 2 × 3P = 6P

⇒ Time for X = 12 months

⇒ Time for Y = 12 − 4 = 8 months

⇒ Time for Z = 12 − 9 = 3 months

⇒ Profit of X = P × 12 = 12P

⇒ Profit of Y = 3P × 8 = 24P

⇒ Profit of Z = 6P × 3 = 18P

⇒ Ratio of Profit (X : Y : Z) = 12P : 24P : 18P = 2 : 4 : 3

⇒ Total ratio parts = 2 + 4 + 3 = 9 parts

⇒ 9 parts = Rs. 450000

⇒ 1 part = 450000 ÷ 9 = Rs. 50000

⇒ Share of Y = 4 parts = 4 × 50000 = Rs. 200000

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 200000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit in Partnership

When partners invest varying capitals for different periods, the profit is divided in the ratio of the product of capital and time. Formula: Profit Ratio = (C₁ × T₁) : (C₂ × T₂).

Working vs Sleeping Partner

A working partner manages the business and receives a salary or fixed percentage of profit as remuneration, whereas a sleeping partner only invests capital and shares the remaining profit strictly according to their investment ratio.

Compound Partnership

If partners alter their investments during the business term by adding or withdrawing capital, the profit distribution is based on the sum of the products of their capital amounts and the respective time periods for which each capital remained invested.

questions.question: The incomes of A and B are in the ratio 5 : 8. If A and B spend ₹36,000 and ₹60,000, respectively, then the ratio of their savings is 3 : 4. What is the savings (in ₹) of B?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Use the **Cross-Multiplication Method** for the **Income ratio** (5 : 8) and **Savings ratio** (3 : 4) with given **Expenditures**.

Difference in cross-products of ratios: |(5 × 4) − (8 × 3)| = |20 − 24| = 4 units.

Difference in cross-products of values: |(3 × 60,000) − (4 × 36,000)| = |180,000 − 144,000| = 36,000.

4 units = ₹36,000 ⇒ 1 unit = ₹9,000.

**Income** of B = 8 units × 9,000 = ₹72,000.

**Savings** of B = Income − Expenditure = 72,000 − 60,000 = ₹12,000.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹12,000.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of **Incomes** of A and B = 5 : 8

**Expenditure** of A = ₹36,000 | **Expenditure** of B = ₹60,000

Ratio of **Savings** of A and B = 3 : 4

**Formula Used:**

**Income** − **Expenditure** = **Savings**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a730fe7c87565135ff7d0b72ee76f672ad95c745b76c70f6c4f56b55df255125.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the **Incomes** of A and B be 5x and 8x respectively.

⇒ Savings of A = 5x − 36,000

⇒ Savings of B = 8x − 60,000

⇒ (5x − 36,000) / (8x − 60,000) = 3 / 4

⇒ 4 × (5x − 36,000) = 3 × (8x − 60,000)

⇒ 20x − 144,000 = 24x − 180,000

⇒ 24x − 20x = 180,000 − 144,000

⇒ 4x = 36,000

⇒ x = 9,000

⇒ **Savings** of B = 8 × 9,000 − 60,000

⇒ **Savings** of B = 72,000 − 60,000 = 12,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹12,000.**

**__Additional Information__**

Income-Expenditure Relationship

The fundamental equation for financial problems is Income = Expenditure + Savings. If any two ratios are given along with absolute values of the third component, the variables can be solved linearly.

Cross-Multiplication Method

For equations of the form (ax − c)/(bx − d) = m/n, the shortcut is |an − bm| units = |nd − mc|. This directly helps in finding the common multiplier 'x'.

Ratio Scaling

Ratios can be scaled by a constant factor without changing the relationship. In income problems, ensure the multiplier is applied to the base income ratio before calculating individual savings or expenditures.

questions.question: Of three positive numbers, the ratio of first and second is 5 : 6 and that of second and third is 9 : 1. The product of first and third number is 480. What is the sum of the three numbers?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Ratio of first and second number = 5 : 6

Ratio of second and third number = 9 : 1

Product of 1st and 3rd number is 480

All three numbers are positive

**Concept Used:**

Concept of ratio and proportion

**Calculation:**

Let, the first two numbers be 5x and 6x.

Second Number : Third Number = 9 : 1

⇒ 2nd number / 3rd number = 9/1

⇒ 3rd number = 2nd number/9

⇒ 3rd number = 6x/9 = 2x/3

Accordingly,

5x × 2x/3 = 480

⇒ (10/3)x² = 480

⇒ x² = 48 × 3

⇒ x = 12 [∵ All numbers are positive, negative value of x should be neglated]

Sum of numbers = 5x + 6x + 2x/3

⇒ 11x + 2x/3

⇒ 11 × 12 + (2 × 12)/3

⇒ 132 + 8

⇒ 140

**∴ The sum of three numbers is 140**

questions.question: In a school library, the ratio of Science to English books is 10 ∶ 13. If there are 400 Science books and due to increase in demand of Science books, few Science books are added by school authority and the ratio becomes 25 ∶ 26. What is the number of Science books added?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Initial ratio of Science to English books = 10 : 13

Number of initial Science books = 400

Ratio after addition of Science books = 25 : 26

**Formula:**

Number of Science books added = Final number of Science books - Initial number of Science books

**Solution:**

From the given initial ratio, 10 parts of the ratio represent 400 books.

⇒ Each part represent 400/10 = 40 books

⇒ So, the number of English books = 13 parts = 40 × 13 = 520 books

Now, the ratio of Science to English books, after addition of Science books, is 25 : 26.

Given, number of English books remain the same (as no addition in English books).

1 part of the ratio is therefore equivalent to 520/26 = 20 books.

⇒ Hence, after addition, the number of Science books = 25 parts = 20 × 25 = 500 books

Number of Science books added = Final number of Science books - Initial number of Science books

⇒ 500 - 400

⇒ 100

**Therefore, the number of Science books added is 100.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/675e2b6d3861a15adb57ada3865382498f3fb3e12925487b480bffa0214b53c4.png] 

**Given:**

Markup Percentage = 25%

Discount Percentage = 8%

**Formula Used:**

MP = CP × (100 + Markup%)/100

SP = MP × (100 − Discount%)/100

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let **CP** = 100 units

⇒ **MP** = 100 × (125/100) = 125 units

⇒ **SP** = 125 × (92/100)

⇒ **SP** = 125 × (23/25) = 5 × 23 = 115 units

⇒ Ratio **SP : CP** = 115 : 100

⇒ Dividing both by 5, Ratio = 23 : 20

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Profit Percentage

The net profit percentage can be calculated using the formula: %Profit = Markup% − Discount% − (Markup% × Discount%)/100.

Relation between CP and MP

CP / MP = (100 − Discount%) / (100 + Profit%). This is useful when profit percentage is given instead of selling price ratio.

Successive Percentage Change

Marking up and then discounting is a form of successive percentage change: Final Factor = (1 + m/100) × (1 − d/100).</p

questions.question: The ratio of prices of coffee and tea is 5 : 7 and the ratio of their quantities consumed by a family is 7 : 9. Find the ratio of expenditures on coffee and tea.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Ratio of prices of coffee and tea = 5 : 7

Ratio of quantities consumed by a family = 7 : 9

Expenditure ratio = Price ratio × Quantity ratio

**Calculation:**

Let the price of coffee be 5x and the price of tea be 7x.

Let the quantity of coffee consumed be 7y and the quantity of tea consumed be 9y.

Expenditure on coffee = 5x × 7y = 35xy

Ratio of expenditures on coffee and tea = 35xy : 63xy

questions.question: An amount of Rs. 5,800 is divided into three parts in such a way that half of the first part, one-fifth of the second part, and three-eighth of the third part are equal. The value of the third part is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Equate the parts: (1/2)A = (1/5)B = (3/8)C

Ratio **A : B : C** = 2 : 5 : 8/3 = **6 : 15 : 8**

Total ratio units = 6 + 15 + 8 = **29 units**

29 units = 5800 ⇒ 1 unit = 200

Third part (8 units) = 8 × 200 = 1600

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 1,600.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total amount = **Rs. 5,800**

Condition: (1/2) × **First Part** = (1/5) × **Second Part** = (3/8) × **Third Part**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a97e34a142e46ff7219e4dabceb64dc6edfcbccd625f570f6187d791e4bb50f7.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the three parts be A, B, and C.

⇒ A/2 = B/5 = 3C/8 = k (say)

⇒ A = 2k, B = 5k, C = 8k/3

⇒ Sum: A + B + C = 5800

⇒ 2k + 5k + 8k/3 = 5800

⇒ 7k + 8k/3 = 5800

⇒ (21k + 8k) / 3 = 5800

⇒ 29k / 3 = 5800

⇒ 29k = 17400

⇒ k = 600

⇒ Third part (C) = 8 × 600 / 3 = 8 × 200 = 1600

Hence, the value of the third part is 1600. Therefore, the correct option is (4).

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 1,600.**

**__Additional Information__**

Ratio Distribution

If a total amount T is divided in the ratio a : b : c, then the value of the third part is calculated as [c / (a + b + c)] × T.

Compound Ratio

The compound ratio of two ratios a : b and c : d is given by (a × c) : (b × d).

Equating Fractions

When fractions of parts are equal (e.g., A/x = B/y = C/z), the parts A, B, and C are directly proportional to the denominators x, y, and z.</p

questions.question: A box consists of 5 rupees, 2 rupees and 1 rupee coins and their total values are in the ratio of 10 : 6 : 3 respectively. If there are total 256 coins, then how many 5 rupees coins are there in the box?

Ratio of total values = 10 : 6 : 3

Ratio of number of coins = (10 ÷ 5) : (6 ÷ 2) : (3 ÷ 1) = 2 : 3 : 3

Total ratio parts for coins = 2 + 3 + 3 = 8 parts

8 parts = 256 coins ⇒ 1 part = 32 coins

Number of ₹5 coins = 2 parts = 2 × 32 = 64

**∴ The correct answer is 64 coins.**

**Given:**

Total number of coins = 256

Denominations = ₹5, ₹2, ₹1

Number of coins = Total Value ÷ Denomination

⇒ Number of ₹5 coins = 10k ÷ 5 = 2k

⇒ Number of ₹2 coins = 6k ÷ 2 = 3k

⇒ Number of ₹1 coins = 3k ÷ 1 = 3k

⇒ Ratio of the number of coins = 2k : 3k : 3k = 2 : 3 : 3

⇒ Total number of coins = 2k + 3k + 3k = 8k

According to the question, total coins are 256:

⇒ 8k = 256

⇒ k = 256 ÷ 8

⇒ k = 32

We need to find the number of ₹5 coins:

⇒ Number of ₹5 coins = 2k = 2 × 32 = 64

**∴ The correct answer is 64 coins.**

Value vs Denomination Concept

Total Value = Number of Coins × Denomination Value. Whenever the value ratio is given, divide it by the denomination to get the coin count ratio.

Given Coin Count Ratio

If a problem provides the ratio of the number of coins instead of the value ratio, multiply the given coin ratio by the respective denominations to obtain the value ratio.

Total Amount Given

If the total amount in rupees is provided instead of the total number of coins, apply the ratio multipliers directly to the value ratio parts to equate their sum to the total given amount.

questions.question: It was intended that Rs. 2,820 be divided among A, B and C in the ratio of 3 : 4 : 5, but by mistake the distributions was made in the proportion of {1over 3}:{1over4}:{1over5}. How much does A gain by the error?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

A's intended share = 3 / (3 + 4 + 5) × 2820 = 3/12 × 2820 = Rs. 705

Mistaken ratio = 1/3 : 1/4 : 1/5 ⇒ 20 : 15 : 12 (multiplying by LCM 60)

A's actual share = 20 / (20 + 15 + 12) × 2820 = 20/47 × 2820 = Rs. 1200

A's gain = Actual share − Intended share = 1200 − 705 = Rs. 495

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 495.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total amount to be divided = Rs. 2820

Intended ratio among A, B, and C = 3 : 4 : 5

Mistaken ratio among A, B, and C = 1/3 : 1/4 : 1/5

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/453b4ce585b618c9a15daee9803e8803dc8bd1979b14cbe34feb14ac8dbb0b27.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Share of individual part = [Individual ratio / Sum of ratios] × Total Amount

**Calculation:**

⇒ Sum of parts in intended ratio = 3 + 4 + 5 = 12

⇒ Intended share of A = (3 / 12) × 2820 = (1 / 4) × 2820 = Rs. 705

⇒ Mistaken fractional ratio = 1/3 : 1/4 : 1/5

⇒ To convert fractions into integers, multiply by the LCM of denominators 3, 4, and 5, which is 60.

⇒ Actual substituted ratio = (1/3 × 60) : (1/4 × 60) : (1/5 × 60) = 20 : 15 : 12

⇒ Sum of parts in actual mistaken ratio = 20 + 15 + 12 = 47

⇒ Actual share received by A = (20 / 47) × 2820 = 20 × 60 = Rs. 1200

⇒ Gain of A caused by the error = Actual received share − Intended share

⇒ Gain = 1200 − 705 = 495

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 495.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Fractional Ratios to Integer Ratios

When a ratio is given in fractional form, simplify it into whole numbers by multiplying each term by the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of all the denominators.

Proportional Distribution

If a total amount T is divided into three parts in the ratio a : b : c, the corresponding values are (a / S) × T, (b / S) × T, and (c / S) × T where S = a + b + c.

Net Change in Share

Gain or Loss is determined by calculating the difference between the actual distributed value and the originally intended value. A positive difference indicates a gain.
